---
title: "API v3 Schema Generation"
description: "Why the v3 Zod schemas are generated from the OpenAPI spec, how the pipeline works, and how to adopt a resource"
icon: "file-code"
---

## Decision

The v3 OpenAPI spec under `docs/api-v3-reference/src/` is the single source of truth for v3 request and
response shapes. Zod schemas and their TypeScript types are **generated from it**, not written by hand and not
the other way round (ENG-3335).

This replaces the earlier plan to generate the spec from Zod with `zod-openapi`, as v2 does. Spec-first keeps
the contract as the reviewed artifact that Schemathesis, Mintlify and the MCP server already read. It also keeps
the prose, examples and error documentation where they live today, and makes contract drift a build failure
instead of something a bespoke drift test may or may not cover.

v2 keeps its code-first `zod-openapi` setup. Only v3 is in scope.

## Generator

`@hey-api/openapi-ts` (MIT) with its `zod` plugin, exact-pinned in `packages/api-v3-schemas`. It was chosen
after running every serious candidate against the real bundle:

| Generator | Result on the v3 bundle |
| --- | --- |
| **hey-api 0.99** | Typechecks, deterministic, smallest install (+11 MB), no telemetry. Faithful once the pipeline below fixes strictness and composition. |
| kubb 5 | Drops a base `required` on `.extend` (an element with no `type` validated), turns an open `metadata` object into `{}`, output fails `tsc`, telemetry on by default. |
| orval 8 | No hook for custom formats (`cuid2`), strictness only all-or-nothing, `z.coerce.boolean` turns `"false"` into `true`. |
| typed-openapi, `z.fromJSONSchema` | Crash on import / throw on `unevaluatedProperties` and `if/then`. |

If hey-api's pre-1.0 churn ever outweighs its fidelity, orval is the fallback, with strictness and `cuid2` moved
into the refinement layer.

## Pipeline

`pnpm api:v3:schemas` runs `packages/api-v3-schemas/scripts/generate.ts`:

<Steps>
  <Step title="Read the committed bundle">
    `docs/api-v3-reference/openapi.yml` — the same file Schemathesis reads, so the schemas and the contract tests
    can never be generated from different inputs.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Scope to the adopted tags">
    `scripts/adopted.ts` lists each tag with its exact operationIds. Only those operations and the components they
    reach are generated, so an edit elsewhere in the contract cannot break the pipeline, and a renamed tag or
    operation fails it instead of silently generating less.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Normalize">
    `scripts/normalize.ts` rewrites the 3.1 idioms hey-api mis-generates: it flattens `allOf` +
    `unevaluatedProperties: false` into one closed object, collapses branches that only carry keywords the
    generator ignores, drops many-to-one discriminator mappings once the members' own enums prove them redundant,
    and strips `readOnly`. What may reach the generator is an **allowlist** of keywords; anything outside it, and any
    recursive schema, throws — a construct the generator silently drops is a validation hole.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Generate and format">
    hey-api runs in memory with two resolvers: `format: cuid2` becomes `z.cuid2()`, and `additionalProperties:
    false` becomes `z.strictObject`. Without the second, unknown keys would be stripped instead of answering 400
    `unsupported_field` — a mass-assignment guard lost. The output is formatted with the repository's Prettier
    config into `src/generated/zod.gen.ts`.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Guards

- **Freshness.** `pnpm lint` runs `pnpm api:v3:check` (bundle vs `src/`) and `pnpm api:v3:schemas:check`
  (generated module vs bundle, byte for byte) on every PR. After editing the spec, `pnpm api:v3:sync` regenerates
  both.
- **Fidelity.** `src/generated.contract.test.ts` diffs the JSON Schema of every generated component and operation
  schema against the spec, path by path: closedness, required, nullability, formats, bounds, enums, union members
  (each one, including duplicates), conditionals (fingerprinted) and closed `allOf` branches that others extend.
  Because JSON Schema shows a `z.unknown()` key as required while Zod accepts it missing, it also asks each required
  key at runtime. It does not model recursion — the normalizer refuses recursive schemas until it does.
- **Pinned gaps.** hey-api cannot express `uniqueItems`, `minProperties`/`maxProperties`, `if/then`, or a required
  key with no type. Each such constraint is pinned in `src/testing/unenforced.ts` with the value the spec states and
  the module that enforces it. The fidelity test fails on any unpinned difference, on a pin whose value moved, and on
  a pin that no longer differs.

## Consuming The Schemas

A route keeps its own small module (Responses: `apps/web/app/api/v3/responses/lib/schemas.ts` and
`resources.ts`) that imports the generated schemas and adds only what they cannot carry:

- refinements for the pinned constraints, with the messages clients read in `invalid_params[].reason`;
- strict parameter objects (`z.strictObject(generated.shape)`), because OpenAPI cannot close a parameter list;
- compositions the generator cannot emit, such as a many-to-one discriminated union rebuilt from the generated
  members (`z.discriminatedUnion("elementType", zResponseAnswer.options)`);
- security declarations such as the ENG-2861 reference manifest.

Query strings are the one exception. A query arrives as strings, sometimes repeated, and bracketed
families such as `filter[finished][eq]` need coercion and repeated-key handling the generated typed schemas do
not do. So `GET /api/v3/responses` and `/count` keep their hand-written parser
(`parse-v3-responses-list-query.ts`), and the generated `zGetResponsesV3Query` / `zCountResponsesV3Query` are
unused until a shared query adapter derives that parsing from them.

Compose first, refine last: Zod 4 refuses to `.extend` over a key once a schema has refinements, and `.refine`
returns a new instance — so anything keyed on schema identity must be attached to the final instance.

## Adopting A Resource

1. Add the tag and its operationIds to `packages/api-v3-schemas/scripts/adopted.ts`, then run `pnpm api:v3:sync`,
   which bundles `docs/api-v3-reference/src/` before generating, so spec edits made for the resource are included.
   If the normalizer throws, extend it deliberately, with a unit test.
2. Pin every new difference the fidelity test reports in `src/testing/unenforced.ts`, naming your module as the
   enforcer.
3. Rebuild the route schemas on the generated ones. Add a counterexample for each pin, a contract diff of each
   route schema, and parse the operation's examples through them (see `write-schemas.test.ts`).
4. **Before generating request bodies, the resource needs a reference-roster test** like Responses'
   `reference-manifest.test.ts`. Generation means a spec edit alone can add an accepted field, top-level or inside a
   nested object such as `meta`; the roster classifies both, by set equality, so it fails until that field's tenancy is
   classified and refuses fields the server derives.
5. Delete the resource's drift test once nothing in it is left that generation does not prove.

## Upgrading The Generator

The version is exact-pinned and the output is committed, so an upgrade is a deliberate PR whose diff shows every
change in the generated code. The fidelity and closedness tests are what catch a regression. The pipeline uses
`ctx.gen.render()` with `dryRun`, which is not a documented API — check it on every bump. A TypeScript or Prettier
catalog bump can also change the formatting and require a regenerate; `pnpm lint` reports it.

The generator is a build-time dependency only. ESLint forbids importing it from `src/`, so no generator code can
reach a served bundle, and a test fails if the generated module ever imports anything but `zod`. The
`@formbricks/api-v3-schemas/testing` entry point reads the bundle from disk and is lint-banned outside tests in
`apps/web`. The pipeline passes an explicit config file that does not exist, so hey-api's loader executes
nothing it finds in the working directory — a test plants a throwing `openapi-ts.config.mjs` and `index.mjs` to keep
it that way. The loader still reads a `.openapi-tsrc` from the working directory — hey-api offers no way to turn that off, and
the file's keys survive wherever the pipeline sets none — so the renderer refuses to run when one is present.

The generator's packages require Node 22.18 or newer, which the repository's Node 24 pin (`engines`, `.nvmrc`, CI
and the Docker image) satisfies. Generator tooling must be under a permissive licence (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD or ISC):
the generated code is part of this AGPL repository, but the tool itself is never distributed.

# v3 API contract tests

[Schemathesis](https://schemathesis.readthedocs.io/) drives a running instance against
[`../openapi.yml`](../openapi.yml) — the committed bundle — and fails when a response violates the
documented status codes, content type, or schema, or when anything answers 5xx. It runs on every PR
via [`.github/workflows/api-v3-contract-tests.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/api-v3-contract-tests.yml)
and is part of the `PR Check Summary` required check.

`api-v3-spec.yml` already lints the source tree and fails on a stale bundle. That proves the
document is well-formed and current; this proves the running API still matches it.

## What is in here

| File                | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `schemathesis.toml` | Phase/timeout config. `[phases.examples] fill-missing` is what makes all 55 in-scope operations run instead of only the few that carry explicit examples. The `[[operations]]` table below it excludes the eight gateway-served Feedback Records operations (see below). |
| `hooks.py`          | Registers the `cuid2` and `web-url` formats and substitutes seeded identifiers, keyed by parameter name and operationId.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `fixtures.json`     | Generated by `db:seed:contract`, gitignored. The id map `hooks.py` reads.                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Coverage is automatic: a newly documented operation is exercised as soon as it is in the bundle. If
its identifiers are not in `fixtures.json` it runs against a generated cuid2 and gets the documented
403 — still a real contract check, just a shallower one. To exercise it against real data, add the
resource in `packages/database/src/scripts/seed-contract-fixtures.ts`.

## Running it locally

Against a dev stack (`pnpm db:up`, app on `localhost:3000`):

```bash
# 1. Seed the base data plus an API key. Any throwaway secret works; nothing is committed.
export SEED_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
pnpm --filter=@formbricks/database db:seed
pnpm --filter=@formbricks/database db:seed:contract

# 2. Run the suite (uv keeps the pinned version out of your global site-packages).
SCHEMATHESIS_HOOKS=docs/api-v3-reference/contract-tests/hooks.py \
  uvx --from 'schemathesis==4.25.0' schemathesis \
  --config-file docs/api-v3-reference/contract-tests/schemathesis.toml \
  run docs/api-v3-reference/openapi.yml \
  --url http://localhost:3000 \
  --phases examples \
  --checks not_a_server_error,status_code_conformance,content_type_conformance,response_schema_conformance \
  -H "x-api-key: fbk_${SEED_API_KEY}"
```

Three things to know before reading the result:

- **Re-run `db:seed:contract` between runs.** The mutating operations consume their fixtures — the
  survey `DELETE` deletes one, `enable` flips another out of `draft`. CI always starts from an empty
  database, so it only matters locally: a second run without re-seeding turns those operations into
  documented 403s and quietly loses depth.

- **Workflow endpoints need an enterprise license.** Thirteen of the forty-five operations (every
  `/workflows` path, the two `/workflows/runs` reads included — they all authorize through
  `buildWorkflowApiContext`), plus `contact-attribute-keys`, `contacts`,
  `contacts/attribute-values` and `segments` (the Contacts entitlement), are entitlement-gated. Without
  `ENTERPRISE_LICENSE_KEY` they answer a documented 403, so the run stays green but tests those
  operations shallowly. A licence is necessary but not sufficient: it also has to _grant_ the
  feature. CI's key grants `contacts` and not `workflows` (ENG-2553), so the 13 workflow operations
  are shallow there too — the job's post-boot probe says which state you are in on every run.
- **Chart and dashboard endpoints need the Dashboards feature.** `db:seed:contract` seeds a Feedback
  Dataset assigned to the seed workspace, charts, dashboards and widgets — one disposable victim per
  mutating operation, with layouts and the save's `expectedUpdatedAt` pinned so each answers its success
  code. Where the licence does not grant Dashboards, every one of them answers the documented 403
  `dashboards_plan_required` instead. The chart data and preview operations answer a documented 502
  either way: the job runs no Cube.
- **Creatives endpoints need a licence with `creatives`.** Without it the fixture workspace, which
  has seeded creatives, is in wind-down: list, get, stats and delete still run against real data, a
  `PATCH` that only pauses or closes runs too, as does the survey-wide pause
  (`/api/v3/creatives/pause`, on a fixture survey of its own), and create, other patches, archive,
  restore and duplicate answer the documented 403 `creatives_not_entitled`. No fixture change is needed
  either way.
- **The four `/tags` operations are session-only** (`auth: "session"`, and the spec declares only
  `sessionAuth`), so an API key gets a documented 401 before any handler runs. They are checked
  against that 401, which is a real assertion that they stay session-only — but no tag fixtures
  exist, because nothing an API key sends can reach them.
- **The eight `/feedbackRecords` operations are not exercised.** They are served by the API gateway
  (Envoy in Cloud, Traefik in the Docker install) straight to the Hub; the Next.js route under
  `/api/v3/feedbackRecords` is a local-dev proxy that needs a running Hub and answers 404 in
  production builds. CI has no Hub, so `schemathesis.toml` disables the `V3 Feedback Records` tag
  rather than test a proxy without an upstream. Their contract is checked by the Hub's own suite and
  the live smoke recorded in ENG-1259. The bundle therefore documents 63 operations and this job
  exercises 55 — the four `/tags` operations carry `x-excluded` (no docs page, ENG-2533) but are
  still tested.
- **The two survey visibility operations answer 403 to every API key** (ENG-3282, K-4), and this
  harness authenticates with one, so `GET`/`POST /api/v3/surveys/{surveyId}/visibility` are checked
  against their documented 403 on a real, readable fixture survey. Their 200/409/422/503 shapes are
  covered by the unit and integration suites. The job marks the survey projection ready
  (`authzed:backfill --scope=survey --apply --mark-ready`) so every other operation runs with
  visibility enforced, then drains the outbox (`authzed:outbox drain`). The fixtures make surveys
  restricted, which queues revocations; with no worker to deliver them, the freshness guard would fail
  every authorization check closed after 60 seconds. Locally, a running dev worker does this for you.
- **Rate limiting.** Set `RATE_LIMITING_DISABLED=1`, otherwise a burst of cases can turn into
  documented-but-uninteresting 429s.

For deeper local exploration, drop `--phases examples` for `--phases coverage` (boundary values) or
`--phases fuzzing -n 50`. Both are far slower than the PR budget allows, which is why CI runs
examples only.

A creative is a feedback button or a banner the web SDK renders on the customer's site; pressing it opens its Destination, a survey or a link. Writes set the author's `status`; reads add the derived `displayStatus`; `stats` returns its daily Impressions and Clicks.

    Creatives needs a self-hosted license that includes it; Formbricks Cloud does not offer it. With one, every operation is available. Without one, a workspace that still has creatives is in **wind-down**: its creatives are no longer shown on sites, and they can only be listed, read (stats included), paused (a PATCH that sets nothing but `status`, or **POST /api/v3/creatives/pause**), closed (the same PATCH) or deleted. A workspace with no creatives has no access at all. Anything not allowed answers **403** `creatives_not_entitled`.

    **Workflows extension**: **GET /api/v3/workflows**, **POST /api/v3/workflows**, **GET /api/v3/workflows/{workflowId}**, **PATCH /api/v3/workflows/{workflowId}**, **DELETE /api/v3/workflows/{workflowId}**, **POST /api/v3/workflows/{workflowId}/duplicate**, **POST /api/v3/workflows/{workflowId}/enable**, **POST /api/v3/workflows/{workflowId}/disable**, **POST /api/v3/workflows/{workflowId}/archive**, **POST /api/v3/workflows/{workflowId}/unarchive**, **POST /api/v3/workflows/{workflowId}/test**, **GET /api/v3/workflows/runs**, and **GET /api/v3/workflows/runs/{runId}**.

    **Charts and dashboards**: charts on a Feedback Dataset (**GET**, **POST /api/v3/charts**; **GET**, **PATCH**, **DELETE /api/v3/charts/{chartId}**; **POST /api/v3/charts/{chartId}/duplicate**), their numbers (**GET /api/v3/charts/{chartId}/data**, **POST /api/v3/charts/preview**), the field catalog (**GET /api/v3/charts/fields**, **GET /api/v3/charts/fields/{field}/values**), and dashboards (**GET**, **POST /api/v3/dashboards**; **GET**, **PATCH**, **PUT**, **DELETE /api/v3/dashboards/{dashboardId}**; **POST /api/v3/dashboards/{dashboardId}/duplicate**; **POST /api/v3/dashboards/{dashboardId}/widgets**; **GET**, **PATCH**, **DELETE /api/v3/dashboards/{dashboardId}/widgets/{widgetId}**).
    - **Field catalog.** A chart query names fields exactly as `GET /api/v3/charts/fields` lists
      them; the validator refuses anything else, and Cube options (`timezone`, `segments`, `ungrouped`,
      …), with **422** naming each problem. Counts, filter depth, `limit` and `offset` are bounded.
    - **Date ranges.** A preset from the catalog's `datePresets`, `all-time`, or two ISO dates, both
      inclusive, read in the organization's time zone. On the data operation a requested range
      replaces the chart's own range on `collectedAt`, the way a dashboard's date filter does.
    - **Data needs the dataset.** Reading a chart's rows, previewing one and looking up field values
      need read access to its Feedback Dataset as well as the workspace. They share one budget of
      **600 per minute** per user or key, sized for dashboards that load one query per widget, and at
      most **20 run at once** (429 with `Retry-After: 1` past that).
    - **Plan.** Every operation answers **403 `dashboards_plan_required`** for an organization without
      the Dashboards feature, after authorization.
    - **Shared charts.** A chart can sit on several dashboards; each chart says which in `dashboards`.
      Editing it changes all of them — duplicate it and repoint one dashboard's widget to change it
      there only. A chart still on a dashboard cannot be deleted: **409 `chart_in_use`** lists them in
      `details.dashboards`.
    - **Grid.** Widgets sit on a 12-column grid in whole units (`1 ≤ w ≤ 12`, `x + w ≤ 12`,
      `1 ≤ h ≤ 8`, `0 ≤ y ≤ 1000`). Gaps are allowed, overlaps answer **422** naming the widget, and a
      chart appears at most once per dashboard (**409**). A widget added without a layout takes the
      first open slot at its chart type's default size.
    - **Stale-check.** `PUT /api/v3/dashboards/{dashboardId}` saves the name and every widget at once
      and removes widgets left out. Send the `updatedAt` you read: if the dashboard changed since,
      nothing is saved and **409** carries `expectedUpdatedAt` and `currentUpdatedAt` in `details`.
      Every widget change moves `updatedAt`.


    Authenticate all management endpoints with **session cookie** or **`x-api-key`** (management key with access to the workspace).

    **Spec location:** source of truth is the multi-file tree at `docs/api-v3-reference/src/` (root `openapi.yml` plus one file per path and component); `docs/api-v3-reference/openapi.yml` is the generated single-file bundle (alongside v2 at `docs/api-v2-reference/openapi.yml`).

    **workspaceId**
    `workspaceId` is the canonical container identifier for this API. It is a **required query parameter on collection read endpoints** (`GET /api/v3/surveys`, `GET /api/v3/action-classes`, `GET /api/v3/contact-attribute-keys`, `GET /api/v3/contacts`, `GET /api/v3/segments`) because those operate within a workspace. **`POST /api/v3/surveys` instead requires `workspaceId` in the request body**, not as a query parameter. Single-resource endpoints (`GET`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/v3/surveys/{surveyId}`) locate the resource by its globally-unique id and resolve the workspace from it, so they do **not** accept a `workspaceId` query parameter — sending one returns **400** with an `invalid_params` entry naming the key itself (`name: "workspaceId"`, `reason: "Unsupported field 'workspaceId'"`), rather than one naming the body.

    **Auth**
    Authenticate with either a session cookie or **`x-api-key`**. In dual-auth mode, V3 checks the API key first when the header is present, otherwise it uses the session path. Unauthenticated callers get **401** before query validation.

    **Pagination**
    Cursor-based pagination with **limit** + opaque **cursor** token. Responses return `meta.nextCursor`; pass that value back as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Survey, contact and segment list responses also include `meta.totalCount`, the total number of items matching the current filters across all pages (`null` when `includeTotalCount=false`). The contact-attribute-key and workflow lists report it only when asked with `includeTotalCount=true`. There is no `offset` in this contract.
    The page-size **maximum is 250** for responses, surveys, action classes, contact attribute keys, contacts and segments; only the *default* varies by resource (20 for surveys, 50 for the workspace reference lists). **The workflows and workflow-run lists remain at 100** — their bound lives in the `packages/workflows` contracts and moves with that package, so each documents the value it actually enforces. A `limit` above an endpoint's maximum is rejected with **400** rather than silently reduced, consistent with v3 rejecting unrecognized query parameters instead of ignoring them. Callers should not infer the end of a collection from a page shorter than `limit`; `meta.nextCursor` of `null` is the only end-of-collection signal. Note that array-valued *input* bounds are a separate concern and stay at 100 — `filter[id][in]` and the batch-delete id list are bounded by write and payload risk, not by page cost.

    **Strictness**
    A query parameter that an operation does not declare returns **400**, with the offending key reported in `invalid_params[].name` — including on operations that declare no query parameters at all. Unknown parameters are rejected rather than ignored on purpose: a silently-dropped filter returns *more* data than the caller believes they asked for, and a typo in a filter name is indistinguishable from no filter at all. The same applies to request bodies, where unsupported fields are rejected instead of stripped.
    Unrecognized **headers** are tolerated, as gateways and proxies legitimately add them; strictness is about parameters and body fields, not transport metadata.
    This is the rule for the surveys, responses, tags and workspace reference-list operations. The workflows family does not enforce it today, so treat parameter strictness there as unspecified rather than guaranteed.
    **Request limits**
    A request body may be at most **2 MB**; a larger one is refused with **413** before it is read. Inside a body, **no array may hold more than 1 000 items, and all arrays together may hold at most 50 000 elements**, at any depth — a body that exceeds either bound is refused with **400** and a single `invalid_params` entry naming the offending array, before any field is validated. The same holds for nesting: a body may nest at most **256** levels of objects and arrays, counted from the root, and a deeper one is refused the same way, naming where it went too deep. Fields with a tighter bound document it as `maxItems` on the field (a survey's `blocks`, `endings`, `variables`, `languages`, `hiddenFields.fieldIds` and `distribution.triggers` since 0.2.0). A 400 or 422 lists at most **50** `invalid_params` entries; when there are more, the last entry says how many were left out. Since 0.2.0.
    **Filtering**
    Filters use explicit operator-style query parameters under the **`filter[...]` family**. The survey list supports `filter[name][contains]`, `filter[status][in]`, and `filter[type][in]`. The workflow list supports `filter[name][contains]` and `filter[status][in]`; the workflow run list supports `filter[status][in]` and `filter[isDryRun][eq]`. Resource-scoping identifiers (`workspaceId`, `workflowId`, `responseId`) stay plain query parameters. Multi-value filters use repeated keys or comma-separated values (e.g. `filter[status][in]=draft&filter[status][in]=inProgress` or `filter[status][in]=draft,inProgress`). Sorting remains a flat `sortBy` query parameter.

    **Responses**
    The response resource is **self-describing**. Answers come back as a typed `answers[]` array in which each entry carries the element's id, label, type and value, rather than as a map keyed by element id — so a consumer holding only a response can read it without fetching the survey and joining. Hidden fields, survey variables and auto-captured context are one `embeddedData[]` collection rather than three parallel concepts, each entry declaring a `kind` and a `type`. Data whose element has since been deleted is reported in `unresolved[]` instead of being dropped silently. Labels are resolved at read time against the current survey definition, and the `resolution` object discloses that policy along with the survey's `updatedAt` so a consumer can detect wording drift.
    Writes take answers in the **stored map form** (`data`) while reads return the typed array. Resolving ids into labelled answers is unambiguous; the reverse would mean matching caller-supplied labels back onto option ids, so the write side keeps the stored shape. To stop that costing round-trippability, the **detailed read returns `data` unchanged** — so a single-response read can be edited and sent back as `PATCH { "data": … }`, and the typed `answers[]` array is an addition rather than a replacement.

    One case where that round trip does not close: a write bound applies to `data` on the way in (`ResponseDataMapInput`) and none applies to the stored map, because v1 and v2 wrote it without one. A response carrying more answer keys than the write accepts therefore cannot be corrected through `PATCH` at all — the whole map is rejected, and sending a smaller one is not a workaround, because `data` is replaced wholesale and every key left out is deleted. Correct those through the v1/v2 management API or the dashboard. This is reachable only on surveys with more elements than the bound allows.
    Embedded Data is the exception, and it is symmetric rather than round-tripped: hidden fields and variables are read and written through `embeddedData`, addressed by **name** in both directions. No raw map of them is echoed, because a name is already what a write accepts — publishing the storage keys underneath (a variable's is its cuid) would expose a layout the caller has no use for. `data` therefore carries element answers only.
    Of those two, only `data` carries no `readOnly`, because it is the same map on the way in and on the way out. Embedded Data is writable through the **request's own** `embeddedData` map, not through the response field of that name — so `embeddedData[]`, like every other derived view on the resource, is marked `readOnly`, per its meaning of server-managed. `ResponseResource` lists them all. The list view omits `data`, since a bulk reader is not editing. `POST /api/v3/responses/validate` exists so a caller can see what a map would produce, and what a write would do, before committing to it.
    `createdAt` and `updatedAt` are **server-owned** on this resource: they cannot be supplied on create or changed by a patch. Response metering counts rows by `(surveyId, createdAt)`, and a client-chosen `createdAt` also lets rows be inserted into the middle of another consumer's already-paginated stream. Backdating stays available on v2 until a dedicated import path exists. The respondent's IP address and the `contactAttributes` snapshot that v1/v2 expose are not part of this resource in any view; that snapshot is copied from the contact at submission time and never refreshed, so it is stale PII by construction.
    Response filtering is allow-listed and index-backed: `filter[createdAt][gte|gt|lte|lt]` (at most one lower and one upper bound — `gte` xor `gt`, `lte` xor `lt`), `filter[finished][eq]`, `filter[language][in]` and `filter[id][in]`. `filter[finished][eq]` and `filter[language][in]` require `surveyId` or `contactId` as well, because both are heap residuals bounded only by an anchored index range. Per-answer, hidden-field, submission-metadata, contact-attribute, quota and tag filters are **not** offered; each is a JSON path or an unindexed join on the largest table in the product. The in-app dashboard does offer them, so this API is knowingly behind the dashboard here — closing the gap requires index work and is tracked separately rather than quietly omitted.
    `GET /api/v3/responses/count` answers "how many match?" directly. The list endpoint's `meta.totalCount` covers a caller that is already paging and is **opt-in** via `includeTotalCount` (default `false`, unlike the survey list) because responses are the highest-cardinality table in the product. Both response counts are **capped at 10 000** and carry an exactness flag — `meta.totalCountRelation` on the list, `data.relation` on `/count` — reading `eq` when the figure is exact and `gte` when the cap was reached and it is a lower bound. An exact count over this table grows superlinearly with the data while a capped one stays flat, so an uncapped total would be the only part of a response whose cost is unbounded. `/count` accepts `precision=exact` for the cases that genuinely need a precise figure, documented as the deliberate slow path. The survey list's `totalCount` stays exact and uncapped: surveys are low-cardinality and that count has a covering index built for it.
    Bulk deletion is `POST /api/v3/responses/batch-delete`, a custom method rather than a collection-level `DELETE`, so a call that loses its filters cannot degrade into erasing everything in scope. It scope-filters rather than rejecting: foreign and already-deleted ids are ignored and the call reports how many rows it removed, which keeps it both leak-free and safe to retry.
    **Security**
    Missing/forbidden workspace returns **403** with a generic message (not **404**) so resource existence is not leaked. Workflow and workflow-run detail endpoints also return **403** for unknown IDs or inaccessible IDs to avoid IDOR leaks. List responses use `private, no-store`.

    **AI survey creation**
    `POST /api/v3/surveys/generate` returns a draft `POST /api/v3/surveys` payload plus validation metadata. It does not create a survey. It generates survey content for both `link` and `app` surveys; for `app` it seeds a default `distribution` (display once, no triggers, no targeting) that you finish configuring before publishing.
    Prompt text is sent to the configured AI provider for generation, but it is not stored by this endpoint, not logged by default, and not included in audit data.

    **Feedback Records** `/api/v3/feedbackRecords` is served by the **API gateway** (Envoy on Formbricks Cloud, Traefik in the one-click Docker install), which authorizes each call against the dataset and forwards it to the feedback store — not by the application routes that serve the rest of v3. Three consequences: the payload is the store's own, so members and filters are **`snake_case`** (`tenant_id`, `value_text`) rather than v3's camelCase; the dataset is named **`tenant_id`** on the wire and is required on every collection operation (it is the feedback dataset id, which the MCP `list_feedback_datasets` tool reports as `dataset_id`); and errors come in two shapes — gateway refusals (**400**, **401**, **403**, **413**, **503**) are `text/plain`, while the store's own problems are `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. These eight operations are the whole of the gateway-served surface; any other path it receives under the prefix answers **400**. Authenticate with **`x-api-key`**: the key needs a permission on a workspace the dataset is assigned to — `read` to list, get and search, `write` to create and update, `manage` to delete — and may update or delete only in a dataset assigned to exactly one workspace.
    **OpenAPI**
    This spec is **not** produced by `pnpm generate-api-specs` (that script only builds v2 → `docs/api-v2-reference/openapi.yml`). When the route contract changes, edit the files under `docs/api-v3-reference/src/`, then run `pnpm api:v3:bundle` to regenerate the committed single-file bundle. `pnpm api:v3:lint` lints the source tree; `pnpm api:v3:check` (CI) fails when the bundle is stale.

    **Workflows Scope 1**
    Workflows are a follow-up extension of the existing v3 Survey API work. The Survey API establishes API-first survey authoring; Workflows build on that same v3 style to automate actions around survey responses through workspace-scoped JSON definitions. Scope 1 models the existing Follow-ups capability as workflows: one `response.completed` trigger with an optional `endingCardIds` filter, and `send_email` actions with Follow-up email field parity. The definition and run shapes mirror the shared Zod schemas in `packages/workflows` (ENG-1100), which are the implementation source of truth for this contract.

    Workflows use `draft`, `enabled`, and `disabled` lifecycle states plus an `archived` soft-delete state. Status only changes through the lifecycle endpoints (`enable`, `disable`, `archive`, `unarchive`); it is not writable via `POST` or `PATCH`. Enabling validates that the definition is executable and snapshots an immutable workflow version; runs reference that snapshot via `workflowVersionId`. `POST .../test` is a dry run: it validates the definition and resolves the trigger's references synchronously, creating no run and sending no email, and returns `{ workflowId, ok, problems }` directly. Real runs execute asynchronously and are polled via `GET /api/v3/workflows/runs/{runId}`.

    **Overview migration note**
    The v3-backed survey overview page intentionally removes actions that are not yet exposed by this contract: `Created by` filtering, `Duplicate`, `Copy...`, `Preview`, and `Copy link`.

    **Next steps (out of scope for this spec)**
    Optional ETag/304, field selection, translation-specific writes, and survey version history.
